title: Arizona water evidence for defensible industrial growth
question: Which records show whether industrial growth has defensible water capacity?
why_it_matters: Industrial strategy in a water-constrained region depends on water rights, provider capacity, reuse, treatment, discharge, drought exposure, and public legitimacy.
current_support: FTFN has ADWR water governance and assured-supply criteria, Phoenix Water Services' April 2026 provider update, a May 2026 Phoenix-TSMC wastewater agreement, and a Project Baccara trail spanning planned chilled cooling and brewery-wastewater reuse plus county conditions requiring an annexation/service agreement or provider will-serve letter and later water-system approvals.
missing_evidence: completed and accepted wastewater conveyance improvements
total facility water withdrawals and consumption
operating industrial reclaimed water plants and measured reuse
candidate_records: next City of Phoenix Water Resource Plan
executed TSMC wastewater development agreement and construction records
facility water balance, discharge, or measured reuse disclosure
Project Baccara service agreement, provider will-serve letter, water-system approvals, measured water balance, discharge, construction, and operating records
next_action: Track completion and acceptance of the TSMC conveyance improvements, operation of the first industrial reclaimed water plant by June 30, 2028, and Project Baccara's service, water-system, construction, and operating records; require measured facility water and reuse evidence before making sufficiency claims.
notes: Phase 55C adds concrete service and water-system prerequisites but no completed water evidence. The gap remains open because planned reuse and permit conditions do not prove a provider commitment, approved source, completed infrastructure, total demand, measured reuse, drought resilience, or long-term sufficiency.
